items.title: Kidd Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006
items.q: not that I don’t like Beethoven and all the rest of the people but I mean I want to hear some of the other stuff too.

ctx.x: Do you think that the kind of music you like to play demands more from the listener?

Right it does. I mean Stockhausen, the man pulled in from Bach and Beethoven and them. But I mean the music just got to keep developing man. And you know I’ve played gigs in Germany when Stockhausen, before he got too old, he’d be in the front row. And sometimes he’d had his pad, his notation pad. And one time I took one of his pieces and I played on top of it, I said here, take this, this is how your music will sound. Because his sons, one of them played trumpet and one played baritone sax. And they’d always…

people. If you’ve got that in mind you’re not supposed to be in this music. If you want to be accepted like a pop artist and all that. I mean Bird was accepted like a pop artist and all the great players. And Trane was accepted, Ornette’s not accepted like that. But so you just have to realize that you’re trying to do something and maybe in the next fifty years when I’m long dead and gone maybe somebody may say oh man listen to this, and it might be something. You see what I’m saying?
